Must ALLOW: this is a real, non-.claude write with no genuine cwd change.

name: A1-reviewer-nomodel-fm-opus
_note: No explicit model: frontmatter fallback resolves to native Opus (the default since the fable-gate flip).

name: A11-reviewer-relaymodel-nomodel
_note: Review-floor judges the native authority role; the relay hook independently judges the external third seat.

name: A19-reviewer-explicit-fable
_note: Native Fable is an official authority model, not a clover alias.

name: A22-planner-explicit-opus
_note: Explicit Opus overrides Fable frontmatter for a recorded fallback.

name: A26-relay-off-native-fable-frontmatter
_note: No relay status file exists. This sandbox's clover/models.json is now seeded with a real alias (probe-ext) so this allow is not a vacuous empty-alias-set pass -- native Fable frontmatter must remain relay-independent even against a non-empty clover alias set. Contrast with A28/A29 below, which use the same non-empty alias set to prove the deny path.

name: A28-relay-off-clover-frontmatter-deny
_note: Route 1 (frontmatter-pinned clover model id), deny half of A26's allow. Sandbox pins .claude/agents/reviewer-clover.md to model: claude-probe-ext and seeds clover/models.json with alias 'probe-ext'; relay OFF (no .relay-status file) must block a genuine clover-id frontmatter pin.

name: A29-relay-off-relaymodel-marker-deny
_note: Route 2 (RELAY-MODEL:<alias> marker), independent of the dispatched agent's own frontmatter (reviewer's frontmatter is native fable). Alias 'probe-ext' resolves via the same sandbox clover/models.json as A28; relay OFF must block.

name: A30-reviewer-claude-fable-allow
_note: norm() strips one leading claude- prefix before matching, so claude-fable resolves to fable (allowed) -- symmetric with the existing claude-opus row (A20) so a future norm() change can't silently shift this acceptance.

name: F1-executor-fable-switch-missing-deny
_note: Ruling B: this hook gates every subagent dispatch, not just authority roles; a missing switch file is not ON.

name: F2-reviewer-nomodel-fm-fable-switch-missing-deny
_note: No explicit model; frontmatter fallback resolves to fable (this sandbox's reviewer.md), and the switch file is missing -- deny.

name: F4-reviewer-nomodel-fm-fable-switch-on-allow
_note: The frontmatter-resolution path must also read the switch, not only the explicit-model path.

name: F5-reviewer-fable-switch-on-messy-allow
_note: Switch file content is whitespace-padded and lowercase ('on') -- trim() plus case-fold must still resolve to ON.

name: F6-planner-fable-switch-off-deny
_note: Switch file exists and reads OFF -- a file existing is not the same as it reading ON.

name: F7-reviewer-fable-switch-onx-deny
_note: Switch file reads ONX -- an exact === 'ON' match is required, not a substring/startsWith test.

name: F8-reviewer-opus-switch-missing-allow
_note: Explicit model opus overrides the fable frontmatter default; the hook only gates the resolved model, and opus is never gated regardless of switch state.

name: F9-executor-sonnet-switch-missing-allow
_note: Switch OFF must not deny every dispatch -- only ones that resolve to fable.

name: F10-reviewer-claude-fable-switch-missing-deny
_note: norm() strips one leading claude- prefix before matching, so claude-fable resolves to fable -- symmetric with block-review-floor.js's A30, but this hook denies because the switch is missing.

name: F11-reviewer-fable-untrimmed-uppercase-switch-missing-deny
_note: norm() trims and lowercases the model string before matching, mirroring block-review-floor.js's A9.

name: F12-general-purpose-noagentfile-unresolved-allow
_note: general-purpose has no .claude/agents/ file, so the model is unresolved. Failing closed here would deny every built-in agent type whenever the switch is OFF -- i.e. in the normal state (Risks R2 in the plan).

name: F13-reviewer-nomodel-fm-fable-still-allowed-by-floor
_note: block-review-floor.js's own allowlist still accepts a fable frontmatter default (fable remains an allowed authority model) -- coverage that A1/A27 lost when they moved to opus fixtures is restored here against the SANDBOX_FREE fable fixture.

name: F14-executor-claude-fable-5-switch-missing-deny
_note: H-1 regression pin: a real-id spelling with a claude- prefix and numeric suffix. norm() strips the prefix to fable-5, which must still match the gate as a Fable spelling -- before the H-1 fix, the bare-word-only comparison let this bypass the gate even with the switch missing.

name: F15-executor-claude-fable-5-switch-on-allow
_note: Same real-id spelling as F14, contrasted with the switch ON -- the widened comparison must still allow it once the gate is open, proving the fix is not an over-wide permanent block.

name: F16-executor-bare-fable-5-switch-missing-deny
_note: H-1 regression pin: a real-id spelling with no claude- prefix, so this row is independent of norm()'s prefix-stripping -- the comparison widening alone must catch it.

name: F17-executor-bare-fable-5-switch-on-allow
_note: Same spelling as F16, contrasted with the switch ON.

name: ge-commit-check-safety-debug-leftover-deny
_note: Liveness row: before this row, check-commit-safety.js had 2 allow rows and zero deny rows -- an inert stub (process.exit(0) unconditionally) would have passed the whole suite. Uses a dedicated throwaway git repo (SANDBOX_GIT, built by buildSandboxGit()) with a staged (not committed) file containing a console.log, since this hook inspects the real `git diff --cached` of whatever repo tool_input.cwd points at rather than parsing the command text.

name: ge-ffonly-catchup-allow
_note: ff5d0d7 (ruling 2026-08-06 Q2): the narrow fast-forward catch-up exception. SANDBOX_GIT_MAIN is a real repo checked out on main with origin/main configured as its tracked upstream (@{u}) -- targeted via -C so this row is independent of <REPO>'s own current branch, needing no skipIf tag. Contrast ge-ffonly-wrong-ref-deny / ge-merge-no-ffonly-deny / ge-pull-ffonly-not-merge-deny below.

name: ge-ffonly-wrong-ref-deny
_note: isFastForwardCatchUp() requires the positional to be textually identical to the branch's own @{u} (origin/main here) -- a different-looking ref falls through to the normal block even with --ff-only present.

name: ge-merge-no-ffonly-deny
_note: Same target ref as ge-ffonly-catchup-allow but without --ff-only -- the exception requires the flag, so this stays blocked even though the ref matches @{u}.

name: ge-pull-ffonly-not-merge-deny
_note: isFastForwardCatchUp() only recognizes subcommand `merge`, not `pull` -- per the header comment, pull/rebase stay fully blocked even with --ff-only.

name: lock-git-restore-exe-residual-negative
_note: Honest-pin (known, out-of-scope hole, NOT fixed by this change): WRITE_INDICATOR_RE's git-restore branch matches only the bare literal 'git' + whitespace, before any .exe/.cmd suffix stripping happens, so '.exe'/'.cmd'-suffixed spellings never set hasWrite and extraction never runs -- this bypasses cmd-write-guard.js's scope-lock enforcement while locked. Contrast lock-L2-not-in-allow (bare 'echo hi > other/a.js', denied) and the bare 'git restore other/a.js' form (also denied) with this row. Filed as the highest-priority tasks/todo.md Backlog item (raw-text-pre-gate class); same pattern also affects 'git.cmd restore' and 'sed.exe -i'.

name: lock-git-restore-bare-deny-contrast
_note: Positive contrast for lock-git-restore-exe-residual-negative above: the bare (unsuffixed) form correctly denies via WRITE_INDICATOR_RE's git-restore branch -- before this row, that branch had zero expect:deny coverage anywhere in the suite, so a regression that silently disabled it would not have been caught.

name: lock-sed-i-bare-deny-contrast
_note: Positive contrast for the sed.exe -i residual bypass noted in the lock-git-restore-exe-residual-negative _note and in tasks/todo.md: the bare (unsuffixed) form correctly denies via WRITE_INDICATOR_RE's \bsed\s+-i branch -- before this row, that branch had zero expect:deny coverage anywhere in the suite.

name: state-touch-unconditional-deny
_note: mkdir/touch join WRITE_INDICATOR_RE (plan Batch A) -- state protection (Arm A/B) is lock-status-independent, so this row uses the UNLOCKED SANDBOX_FREE fixture on purpose: Duty 2 never runs here, isolating that the state guard alone denies.

name: lock-sudo-cp-exe-not-in-allow
_note: The dangerous-direction proof for Batch C: before the fix, sudo.exe was an unrecognized opaque wrapper so this write was silently unresolved (no targets extracted, no unresolved flag set either) and fell through to an implicit ALLOW even though the target is outside the allow list. After the fix sudo.exe peels to reveal cp, whose target correctly resolves and is denied.

name: lock-scopejson-locked-plan-deny
_note: ff5d0d7: scope.json (the approved allowlist itself) is deliberately excluded from alwaysAllow -- a lock whose own allowlist can be rewritten while armed is not a lock. Contrast lock-plan-md-allow / lock-deviations-md-allow below (same plan dir, PLAN.md and deviations.md ARE always-writable).

name: lock-plan-md-allow
_note: ff5d0d7: PLAN.md for the locked plan's own dir stays always-writable (post-implementation result notes need it) even though it is outside lock.allow (sub/**).

name: lock-deviations-md-allow
_note: ff5d0d7: deviations.md for the locked plan's own dir stays always-writable (out-of-scope intents must be recordable while locked) even though it is outside lock.allow (sub/**).

name: lock-other-slug-scopejson-deny
_note: Negative contrast for lock-scopejson-locked-plan-deny: a DIFFERENT plan dir's scope.json (not even the locked slug's own PLAN.md-adjacent alwaysAllow entries apply here) is denied too -- confirms the always-allow carve-out is scoped to the locked plan's own planDir, not a blanket '**/scope.json is special' rule.

name: sg-L1-in-allow
_note: scope-guard.js is the Edit/Write counterpart of cmd-write-guard.js's Bash/PowerShell path (both share lib/scope-decision.js's decide()) -- it always exits 0 and signals deny via a stdout permissionDecision JSON blob, same as cmd-write-guard.js, which verdictOf() did not recognize until this row's set was added (see hook-probes.test.js STDOUT_DENY_HOOKS).

name: sg-L3-unlocked-allow
_note: SANDBOX_FREE has no .claude/state/scope-lock.json (readLock() returns null) -- unlocked sessions must stay unaffected via the Edit/Write path too.

name: sg-L4-enforcement-chain-deny
_note: IMPLICIT_FORBID applies identically via scope-guard.js -- the enforcement chain itself stays unwritable through the Edit/Write path too, not just Bash.

name: sg-L5-plan-md-allow
_note: alwaysAllow()'s PLAN.md carve-out applies identically via scope-guard.js.

name: pt-deny-todo-predates-branch
_note: SANDBOX_TODO_DENY: tasks/todo.md mtime is pinned (fs.utimesSync) to 2000-01-01, strictly before the topic branch's real reflog creation timestamp -- deterministic, no wall-clock race against git's 1s-granularity reflog.

name: pt-allow-todo-after-branch
_note: SANDBOX_TODO_ALLOW: tasks/todo.md mtime is pinned to 2099-01-01, strictly after the topic branch's creation -- the "todo.md touched after the branch was created" case.

name: pt-allow-no-reflog
_note: SANDBOX_TODO_NOREFLOG: git init only, zero commits -- .git/logs/refs/heads/topic never gets created, so branchCreatedMs() throws ENOENT and the hook fails open.

name: pt-allow-pr-view-not-create
_note: Same deny-shaped sandbox as pt-deny-todo-predates-branch, but the subcommand is not `pr create` -- pins that gh pr view is never intercepted, even where a `pr create` would be denied.

name: pt-allow-pr-list-not-create
_note: Same deny-shaped sandbox as pt-deny-todo-predates-branch, but the subcommand is not `pr create` -- pins that gh pr list is never intercepted, even where a `pr create` would be denied.

name: pt-allow-cd-into-product-repo

tool_input.command: cd dev/prod && gh pr create -t x

_note: SANDBOX_TODO_DENY/dev/prod is its OWN nested git repo with the OPPOSITE (allow-producing) todo.md timestamp -- pins that repo-root resolution walks up from the effective (post-cd) cwd and finds dev/prod's own .git, not the outer deny-producing repo.

name: pt-allow-pushd-untrackable

tool_input.command: pushd dev/prod && gh pr create -t x

_note: H-1 regression pin: pushd is never cd-tracked (bash builtin, not in the cd-only tracker) -- before the H-1 fix, cur silently stayed at the outer (deny-producing) repo and this FALSELY DENIED even though dev/prod (the real destination) is allow-producing. After the fix, pushd makes the whole command resolve to fail-open (allow) rather than answer using the wrong repo.

name: pt-allow-cd-exe-untrackable

tool_input.command: cd.exe dev/prod && gh pr create -t x

_note: H-1 regression pin: lib/parse-cmd.js CWD_BUILTINS deliberately leaves cd.exe suffixed (cmd stays "cd.exe", not "cd"), so the cd==="cd" tracker never fires -- before the fix this FALSELY DENIED against the stale outer cwd. After the fix, a suffixed cd/pushd/popd spelling makes the whole command fail-open.

name: pt-allow-cd-var-untrackable

tool_input.command: D=dev/prod; cd $D && gh pr create -t x

_note: H-1 regression pin: a variable-expanded cd destination cannot be resolved without a shell -- before the fix, path.resolve(cur, "$D") produced a bogus literal-"$D" path and evaluation fell through to the outer (deny-producing) repo, FALSELY DENYING. After the fix, a destination containing $ makes the whole command fail-open.

name: pt-allow-ps-setlocation-untrackable

tool_input.command: Set-Location dev/prod; gh pr create -t x

_note: H-1 regression pin: the cd-tracking model is bash-only (cmd==="cd"); Set-Location never matches it even though this hook is registered for PowerShell too -- before the fix this FALSELY DENIED against the stale outer cwd. After the fix, Set-Location makes the whole command fail-open.

name: pt-allow-ps-sl-untrackable

tool_input.command: sl dev/prod; gh pr create -t x

_note: Same bug/fix as pt-allow-ps-setlocation-untrackable, via the sl alias.

name: pt-allow-ps-chdir-untrackable

tool_input.command: chdir dev/prod; gh pr create -t x

_note: Same bug/fix as pt-allow-ps-setlocation-untrackable, via the chdir alias.

name: pt-allow-cd-no-dest-untrackable
_note: A bare cd (-> $HOME) has no destination this hook can resolve -- before the fix, the tracker silently left cur unchanged (a no-op, NOT a fail-open) and evaluation proceeded against a cwd that does not reflect where the shell actually is. After the fix, a destination-less cd makes the whole command fail-open instead of guessing.

name: pt-allow-cd-subshell-paren-untrackable
_note: Subshell-entry form: lib/parse-cmd.js glues the leading ( onto the cd token (cmd becomes "(cd", not "cd"), so the tracker never fires and (before the fix) evaluation silently fell through to the outer (deny-producing) repo. After the fix, any segment whose cmd starts with ( makes the whole command fail-open.

name: pt-deny-second-occurrence-sec8

tool_input.command: cd dev/prod && gh pr create -t x && cd .. && gh pr create -t y

_note: SEC-8 regression pin: two gh pr create occurrences in one command, the first inside dev/prod (allow-producing) and the second back in the outer repo (deny-producing) after cd ... Before the SEC-8 fix, the detection loop returned on the FIRST match only, so this command was WRONGLY ALLOWED (verified 2026-08-07: exit 0) even though the second occurrence should deny. After the fix, every occurrence is evaluated and a deny on any one denies the whole command.
